meta_quotes.quote: SALESFORCE, INC. SOC 2 REPORT FOR SLACK TEAM COLLABORATION PLATFORM A TYPE 2 INDEPENDENT SERVICE AUDITOR’S REPORT ... NOVEMBER 1, 2024, TO OCTOBER 31, 2025
Non-specified users may not rely on this report and do not acquire any rights against Schellman & Company, LLC as a result of such access.

3.1.1.quote: Encrypt data in transmission using transport layer security (TLS) or other technologies over public networks.
3.1.1.note: No TLS version stated anywhere, so no exact dropdown match. Tested control 6.06: 'Data transmitted between the public Internet and production servers is encrypted.' (p. 37).

3.1.2.detail: AES (key length not specified in report)
3.1.2.quote: Confidential data stored within the production services utilize advanced encryption standard (AES) encryption.
3.1.2.note: AES is stated but no key length (128/192/256) appears in the report, so none of the exact dropdown values match. Tested control 6.07: 'Sensitive customer data is encrypted at rest.' (p. 37).

3.1.4.quote: EKM customer message and file data is encrypted at rest with Customer's encryption keys.
3.1.4.note: Applies only to the optional Enterprise Key Management (EKM) feature. For default at-rest encryption the report does not state who generates the keys, so without EKM the answer would be 'Not known'.

value: Two-factor authentication required for production environment, source code, and hosting provider interfaces (SOC 2 p. 13)
Firewalls and multi-factor authentication isolate development/production environments from the Internet (p. 13)
Vulnerability management, automated scanning, penetration tests, and a bug bounty program (p. 13)
Full-disk encryption and security-patch currency required on company devices (p. 13)
Production hosted across multiple geographically diverse availability zones; recovery from backup practiced at least every 90 days (pp. 11, 20)
User data replicated in real time between two database instances and backed up nightly, with backup-failure alerting (p. 40)

quotes.quote: Two-factor authentication is required to access the production environment, source code, hosting provider interfaces
The development and production environments use firewalls and multi-factor authentication to isolate themselves from the Internet.

Vulnerability management, automated scanning, penetration tests, a ‘bug bounty’ program, restrictive firewalls, and strong encryption of data transmitted over the public Internet are among the security measures employed by the Company.
Devices issued to Company personnel must meet minimum security criteria that include being locked when unattended, employing full-disk encryption
at least every 90 days, the Company practices recovery from backup, as would occur in the case of a complete failure
user data was automatically replicated in real- time between two database instances and backed up on a nightly basis

absent_notes.3.1.3: Backups are addressed (Amazon S3 stores backup copies of customer data, p. 12; nightly database backups, p. 40) but the report never states an encryption standard for backups.
absent_notes.3.1.6: No mention of anonymization anywhere in the report.
absent_notes.3.1.7: No mention of pseudonymization anywhere in the report.
absent_notes.3.2.1: No EU region or data-center location stated; the report only says production cloud infrastructure is 'hosted within multiple geographically diverse availability zones / regions' (p. 11) on AWS.
